subject.title: [Feature]: Support sessionKey-based concurrency guard for webhook       deliveries

question: Should hook-agent deliveries with the same resolved `sessionKey` be rejected, skipped, queued, or remain parallel by default, and should any `409` behavior be opt-in?
rationale: The requested behavior changes an external webhook HTTP response contract and retry semantics, so automation cannot safely choose the default or compatibility policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add opt-in overlap policy
options.body: Keep current accepted-by-default behavior and add documented reject, skip, or queue semantics that trusted hook mappings or callers can opt into.

options.title: Make 409 the default
options.body: Reject same-session active deliveries by default, accepting that existing webhook integrations may need migration to avoid retry storms.

options.title: Fold into queued ingestion
options.body: Treat this as part of the broader queued webhook design and do not add a separate 409 guard until that core queue policy is decided.

recommendation.title: Add opt-in overlap policy
recommendation.body: Keep current accepted-by-default behavior and add documented reject, skip, or queue semantics that trusted hook mappings or callers can opt into.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest history signal for hook/session policy and prior product/security framing of this exact decision.
